text:
ashley: hey team, saw a spike of GPU errors on cluster-prod-eu1 this morning, flagged by infra-bot
miguel: what kind of errors? ECC/Xid/temperature?
ashley: Xid 13 and ECC correctable counts on 3 different cards on node gpunode-eu1-12 within ~10m
infra-bot: ALERT: gpu_error_rate{node="gpunode-eu1-12",gpu="gpu0"} > 0 for 1m — severity=warning
kai: ugh, those nodes are on the older A40s, we've been seeing intermittent soft ECCs since the kernel upgrade
devon: can you paste the recent logs / prometheus snippet?
ashley: here's a short dump:

```
# node-exporter logs
2026-03-12T09:10:21Z dcgm_exporter: dcgm_ecc_correctable_total{gpu="gpu0"} 7
2026-03-12T09:11:03Z dcgm_exporter: dcgm_xid_occurrence_total{gpu="gpu0",code="13"} 2
2026-03-12T09:15:00Z kubelet: pod preempted on gpunode-eu1-12
```

miguel: thanks. sounds like bursty, not sustained. our current prometheus rule fires on any nonzero in 2m which is too sensitive.
kai: agreed. proposal: add a 5m window and require either >3 XIDs or >10 ECC corrections across GPUs on the same node. Also add per-gpu hysteresis so single transient doesn't escalate.
ashley: +1. want to also group by gpu index and by vendor/model, since some models produce noisy correctables but are harmless.
devon: rough rule change I tested locally:

```
- alert: GPU_ECC_ERRORS
- expr: increase(dcgm_ecc_correctable_total[2m]) > 0
- for: 2m
+ alert: GPU_ECC_ERRORS
+ expr: sum by (node) (increase(dcgm_ecc_correctable_total[5m])) > 10
+ for: 5m
+ labels:
+   severity: page
+ annotations:
+   summary: "High aggregate ECC correctables on {{ $labels.node }}"
```

miguel: sounds right. for XIDs do something similar but differentiate code 13 vs code 31 (code 13 is usually kernel recoverable, 31 is more serious):

```
alert: GPU_XID_HIGH
expr: sum by (node,code) (increase(dcgm_xid_occurrence_total[5m])) > 3
for: 5m
```

kai: also add a lower-severity alert for single-gpu flares to monitor trends without paging. e.g., severity=warning if per-gpu >2 in 10m, severity=page if node aggregate >3 in 5m.
ashley: ops question — when we page, do we auto-drain? current playbook suggests manual confirm after triage.
devon: prefer manual for now. auto-drain caused collateral earlier when noisy cards recovered. playbook tweak: add explicit step to check microcode/kernel pairing, then manual cordon/drain.
ashley: can we also add a short-term suppression during kernel upgrades? many of these clusters had rolling kernel updates last week.
miguel: yep, infra-bot can annotate maintenance windows and suppress alerts via the alertmanager silence API. I'll add a job that flips a silence label for nodes in maintenance.
kai: one more thing: add a rate-limited alert route so multiple similar page alerts within 30m are grouped and only top-2 nodes escalate.
devon: good call. routing example for alertmanager:

```
route:
  receiver: "on-call"
  group_by: ["alertname","cluster","node"]
  group_wait: 30s
  group_interval: 30m
  repeat_interval: 4h
  routes:
    - matchers: ["severity=page"]
      continue: false
```

ashley: who owns the rollout of these rule changes? I can PR and run smoke tests in staging.
miguel: assign to @miguel for review, @kai for validation on model grouping, then @sre-lead for approval to prod.
sre-lead: I'm fine with the approach. add unit tests for the prometheus expressions and a dashboard tile showing per-node aggregate so on-call can eyeball noisy nodes quickly.
infra-bot: NOTE: created ticket INFRA-4021 for follow-up (link: https://issues.redwood-inference.internal/INFRA-4021)
ashley: I'll open the PR today, include the sample rules + alertmanager routing + updated playbook snippet.
kai: small to-do: update the `dcgm_exporter` metric docs to clarify labels and version where noisy correctables were introduced.
devon: and let's add a probe in our rollout pipeline: when kernel or dcgm_exporter changes, run a simulated spike test using the testbed to ensure no pager storms.
ashley: thanks all. plan: PR by EOD, staging test tomorrow, prod rollout after SRE signoff. :thumbsup:
miguel: thanks, tagging @oncall for visibility
oncall: noted — will watch for new alerts after rollout. :eyes:
